chunks: And in the narration of Jَمِيل from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, he said:
Regarding the tooth of a child: a man strikes it, so it falls out, then it grows back. He عليه السلام said: “There is no qisas against him, but arsh is upon him.”
And he عليه السلام said regarding a man whose hand is broken, then his hand heals: “Retaliation is not carried out against him, but arsh is given.”
And Jamil was asked: how much is the arsh for the tooth of the child and the breaking of the hand? He said: “A small amount.”

key_terms.الْأَرْشُ: financial compensation assessed for an injury short of full fixed diyah
key_terms.قِصَاصٌ: legal retaliation in cases of bodily injury

ai.seo_question: If an injured tooth or broken hand heals, is qisas still applied or only arsh paid?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on bodily injury when the damaged limb or tooth later recovers or grows back. In such cases, qisas is not applied; instead, a reduced financial compensation, namely arsh, is due. It indicates that compensation is assessed in light of the remaining harm rather than the original injury alone.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5298 - In the narration of Jameel from some of our companions from one of the Imams (peace be upon them), that it was reported regarding the tooth of a child that is struck by a man and falls out but later grows back
Imam (as) said: "There is no retaliation (qisas) upon him, but he must pay compensation (arsh)."
Regarding a man whose hand is broken but later heals,
Imam (as) said: "There is no retaliation against him, but he must pay compensation (arsh)."
When Jamil was asked about the amount of compensation for the child's tooth and the broken hand, Imam (as) replied: "It is a small amount"
